items.title: Migration, crypto and red tape to feature in budget bid for economic growth
items.description: Treasurer Jim Chalmers says Australia's productivity problem will take a long time to fix, but a $10 billion annual saving on business compliance costs is a start.

items.title: Chinese oil tanker hit in reportedly first attack since Hormuz crisis
items.description: The chief engineer of a Chinese-owned oil tanker attacked near the Strait of Hormuz says it is "still unclear" who fired on the vessel.

items.title: US expects Iranian response on proposal to end war within hours
items.description: Iran and the US exchanged fire after weeks of relative calm in the Middle East, with each side claiming the other initiated the violence.

items.title: Police told to switch bodycams to flight mode to avoid detection by criminals
items.description: Thousands of police officers have been advised to disable the bluetooth on their Axon body-worn cameras during raids and undercover jobs to avoid being detected and tracked, after Four Corners exposed a security flaw with the devices.

items.title: 'We don't want the penalty': Moses wins the game but doesn't end it
items.description: Mitchell Moses stuns the Cowboys in a bizarre golden-point finish, after Parramatta crosses twice in the final six minutes of normal time.

items.title: 'I don't coach for my job': Voss defiant after latest loss, Dogs edge Port
items.description: Carlton coach Michael Voss is frustrated after a close loss to Brisbane, but denies he is coaching for his job, while the Western Bulldogs hold off Port Adelaide despite being held to one goal in the second half.

items.title: 'Spat in my face', 'scared for my life': Testimonies from antisemitism commission's first week
items.description: This week, the Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion has heard testimony from Jewish Australians about their lived experiences.

items.title: Probe makes adverse findings against former ANU Council members
items.description: An independent review into 36 allegations concerning the Australian National University has made a series of adverse findings against former council members.

items.title: Anika Wells repays $10,000 in travel costs that broke rules
items.description: An audit of Communications and Sports Minister Anika Wells's travel by the Independent Parliamentary Expenses Authority found four breaches, but cleared her controversial trips to New York and Thredbo.

items.title: What is known about the IS-linked families that arrived in Australia
items.description: Women and children linked to the Islamic State terrorist group have arrived in Melbourne and Sydney. Here's who they are and what awaits them.

items.title: Plaintiff's lawyer describes Rebel Wilson as 'fantastical liar' in court
items.description: Final arguments in the defamation trial between Charlotte MacInnes and Rebel Wilson have heard claims of a suspicious career jump to "terrible, terrible" allegations.

items.title: Students receive ransom messages after learning system cyberattack
items.description: Hundreds of thousands of students have been unable to access schoolwork or submit assessments as access to Canvas has been paused.

items.title: Removing capital gains tax discount will be 'disastrous' for startups
items.description: Some entrepreneurs argue any changes to reduce the capital gains tax discount should carve out the start-up sector. However, tax experts warn this would create too much complexity in an already complicated tax system.

items.title: Three hikers killed in volcano eruption in Indonesia with 17 others rescued
items.description: Mount Dukono erupted on Friday morning, local time, sending plumes of ash some 10 kilometres into the sky.

items.title: Japan confirms first fatal bear attack this year with two more suspected
items.description: Japanese authorities say a 55-year-old woman found dead last month was killed by a bear. It is the first confirmed fatal bear attack for 2026 following a record 13 deaths last year.

items.title: Portrait of elder and artist wins Archibald prize in unanimous vote
items.description: The Melbourne-based artist painted Pitjantjatjara elder Iluwanti Ken, who is known for her large-scale drawings and was also a finalist in this year's Wynne Prize.

items.title: Mother's Day can reopen painful wounds. Here's how to start healing
items.description: It's the yearning ache that comes from reckoning with the imperfect human mother we get, against the idealised fantasy version we wish for.

items.title: Beyonce's hip-hop film debut walked so that Hamilton could fly
items.description: Carmen: A Hip Hopera starred superstar Beyonce in her acting debut. It's been 25 years since the now cult classic musical drama aired on MTV in the United States.

items.title: Bin night across Australia is changing as councils, households fight waste
items.description: How councils collect rubbish is changing as the cost of disposing of waste skyrockets and they scramble to meet environmental targets.

items.title: SA premier 'very concerned' over Whyalla steelworks' blast furnace
items.description: Whyalla steelworkers are struggling to get the city's blast furnace producing iron again, with SA Premier Peter Malinauskas saying he is "very concerned" about the situation.

items.title: NT taxpayers to be hit with $75m bill if fracking project fails
items.description: Northern Territory taxpayers will be hit with a $75 million bill if Tamboran Resources, one of the key Beetaloo Basin fracking companies, is unable to repay its lenders.

items.title: Dozens charged over seizure of largest child porn stash in NSW history
items.description: A probe into a cloud-based image-sharing folder resulted in the largest amount of child abuse material files seized in a single investigation in NSW history.

items.title: Israeli money launderer found guilty in Sydney investment scam trial
items.description: Israeli citizen Shabtay Yaacoby is found guilty of laundering more than $10 million stolen by investment scammers.

items.title: Aussie teen returns from injury to race in new Italian championship
items.description: Teenager Aiva Anagnostiadis, a rising star of Australian motorsport, is hoping to leave a difficult end to 2025 in her rear view as she prepares for her newest challenge in Italy.

items.title: E-bike 10km/h limit in Qld should be watered down, committee says
items.description: A proposed 10km/h speed limit for e-mobility on footpaths should only apply in high pedestrian zones and not on shared paths, a Queensland parliamentary committee has recommended.
